subjects.displayTitle: Piety: reverence that becomes trustworthy conduct
subjects.introduction: Fear usually makes a life smaller. The fear of God that Bahá’u’lláh calls true piety does the opposite: the one who fears none but God is released from fear of kings, crowds and consequences, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that this fear is not dread of punishment but dread of losing the Lord’s loving-kindness. It works as an inward guardian, restraining a person outwardly and inwardly where laws and reputations restrain only the surface, and Bahá’u’lláh names it the commander whose hosts are an upright character and goodly deeds. Its evidence is never private: truthfulness on the tongue, generosity in the hands, courtesy, fairness and restraint, a fortress sheltering the peoples of the world. Qur’an 2:177 describes the same righteousness in practical terms, joining belief and prayer with giving to orphans and travellers, keeping one’s word and bearing hardship patiently [1]. From here the way runs into the love of God that gives this reverence its warmth, into purity of heart and sincerity of intention, and along the spiritual path, where contentment shows what it is to trust the One you revere.
subjects.arc: Begin with freedom from worldly fear and love of divine grace, examine the inward guardian of conduct, then follow justice, restraint, worship, and steadfastness into practical character.

order.why: Contrast outward deterrence with an inward guardian of conduct.
Open with fear of God joined to freedom from fear of earthly powers.
Read the distinction between fear of pain and deprivation of divine loving-kindness.
Make trustworthiness, truthfulness, and courtesy visible as expressions of reverence.
shortened: O people of the world! Follow not the promptings of the self, for it summoneth insistently to wickedness and lust; follow, rather, Him Who is the Possessor of all created things, Who biddeth you to show forth piety, and manifest the fear of God.

Adorn your heads with the garlands of trustworthiness and fidelity, your hearts with the attire of the fear of God, your tongues with absolute truthfulness, your bodies with the vesture of courtesy. These are in truth seemly adornings unto the temple of man, if ye be of them that reflect.

order.why: Read tolerance and righteousness together as educators.
shortened: This Wronged One exhorteth the peoples of the world to observe tolerance and righteousness, which are two lights amidst the darkness of the world and two educators for the edification of mankind.

order.why: Consider generosity, dignity, courtesy, love, and remembrance as concrete adornments.
Read the call for knowledge crowned with deeds, fairness, love, and justice.
Connect a person’s elevated station with character that educates the world.
shortened: Lofty is the station of man, were he to hold fast to righteousness and truth and to remain firm and steadfast in the Cause. In the eyes of the All-Merciful a true man appeareth even as a firmament; its sun and moon are his sight and hearing, and his shining and resplendent character its stars. His is the loftiest station, and his influence educateth the world of being.

Verily I say, fear of God is the greatest commander that can render the Cause of God victorious, and the hosts which best befit this commander have ever been and are an upright character and pure and goodly deeds.

order.why: Read the extended account of fear of God as the commander of good deeds and justice.
shortened: The first word which the Abha Pen hath revealed and inscribed on the first leaf of Paradise is this: "Verily I say: The fear of God hath ever been a sure defence and a safe stronghold for all the peoples of the world. It is the chief cause of the protection of mankind, and the supreme instrument for its preservation. Indeed, there existeth in man a faculty which deterreth him from, and guardeth him against, whatever is unworthy and unseemly, and which is known as his sense of shame. This, however, is confined to but a few; all have not possessed, and do not possess, it.

We have admonished Our loved ones to fear God, a fear which is the fountain-head of all goodly deeds and virtues. It is the commander of the hosts of justice in the city of Baha. Happy the man that hath entered the shadow of its luminous standard, and laid fast hold thereon.

order.why: Consider the stated relation between religion, restraint, and public welfare.
Read security, comfort, and mercy as intended consequences.
Connect triumph through reverence with security and tranquility.
Keep justice, equity, chastity, and trustworthiness within the source’s claim about religion.
Hear the concise statement concerning preservation of human dignity.
shortened: The purpose of all they have spoken and taught was, in one respect, the preservation of human dignity and station.

order.why: Read the discussion of wisdom, rights, reward, and punishment.
shortened: Glory be to Him Who spoke this supreme word: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God," for the fear and awe of God restraineth man from whatsoever causeth abasement and degradation of the human station, and aideth him in that which leadeth to elevation and glory. The wise man avoideth shameful deeds, for he beholdeth punishment in their wake. The pavilion of world order is upheld upon two pillars: Reward and Punishment.

order.why: Keep the explicit language of punishment and justice beside other accounts of fear.
shortened:
The essence of wisdom is the fear of God, the
dread of His scourge and punishment, and the apprehension
of His justice and decree.

order.why: Retain the question about four schools of thought and accountability in its preserved form.
Read the reported comparison of outward law and inward prevention.
Keep the reported distinction between divine fear and concern for reputation.
shortened: Those who are god-fearing never commit such things and those people who are not afraid of God are most considerate lest they might jeopardize their reputation and good name and thus be degraded in the estimation of the public and bring disgrace upon themselves and upon those who are connected with them in the business world.

order.why: Consider piety as restraint in the explanation of the Quranic promise.
Read prevention of spiritual harm through the analogy of guarding health.
Consider refinement both outward and inward.
shortened: The fear of God hath ever been a sure fortress for the protection of the commanding self. It is the cause of the refinement and sanctification of one's being, both outwardly and inwardly.

order.why: Read righteousness and piety as protective armor.
Follow the imagery of lamp, strength, companion, and fortress.
Read cleansing desire and the conquest of hearts through the source’s martial imagery.
Keep the hosts of deeds and character together with wisdom.
Read the pure-deeds image and the guardian of those hosts.
shortened: No host hath been or is mightier than pure deeds and radiant character, and the guardian and leader of these hosts hath ever been and shall ever be the fear of God.

order.why: Consider the opening of cities in its spiritual vocabulary.
shortened: And We counsel all to the fear of God. It is the opener of cities and it is the helper of truth and the succourer, and it is the protector of the friends and their helper.

order.why: Read the standard of piety alongside the rejection of transgression.
shortened: O Ba'i, upon thee be the Glory of God! Hearken unto the counsel of God and give ear to His commandments, and convey them, saying: O friends of God! The standard of piety hath ever been victorious and triumphant. Hold ye fast unto it. Verily, He commandeth you to righteousness and piety, and forbiddeth you transgression and wickedness.

order.why: Return to righteousness and fear of none except God.
Keep the Four Valleys’ paradox of fear in its quoted form.
Consider the stated sweetness of reverence.
shortened: As to what you wrote describing the friends in that land - We bear witness to what you have witnessed, but We counsel them to fear God, your Lord and the Lord of the worlds. For through fear of God the greatness of the Cause and the sanctification of Truth have been and continue to be made manifest among creation. By My life! If anyone were to taste the sweetness of the fear of God, they would hold fast to it all their days.

order.why: Read the lamp and garment imagery through detachment.
shortened: Today the fear of God is as a lamp, and it is the first light that hath shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of detachment, and it is the greatest and most gracious robe for the temples of His servants. Blessed is the head adorned thereby and the temple that hath attained unto it.

order.why: Consider piety and detachment together as lights of teaching.
Consider the luminous garment in the personal address.
shortened: Cling ye unto the fear of God in His religion. By My life! It is My garment - blessed is he who attains unto this luminous garment.

order.why: Read character as garment and fear of God as crown.
shortened: No garment hath been or is more excellent for the temple of man than goodly character, and no crown better than the fear of God.

order.why: Keep the parallel adornment image as its own source.
shortened: From the murmuring of the Kawthar of the Merciful's utterance, this blessed word was heard: No adornment hath ever been or will ever be more excellent for the temple of man than the fear of God, and no garment more befitting than upright character.

order.why: Connect the crown of detachment with the temple of existence.
shortened: Adorn the head of acceptance with the crown of detachment and the temple of existence with the fear of God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Read the prayer for detachment and righteousness.
Consider the attributed radiance of a person’s detachment and piety.
shortened: I testify that through your detachment the sun of detachment hath shone forth from the horizon of creation, and through your God-fearingness the light of piety hath beamed forth amidst all beings.

order.why: Hear the concise relation between piety and manifested light.
shortened: Through piety doth the light of Baha appear - hold fast unto it, O concourse of companions!

order.why: Read the handhold and ladder as images of approach.
shortened: Hold fast to the handhold of godliness - verily it is the ladder unto the source of names and attributes.

order.why: Consider submission, contentment, help, and deliverance together.
Retain the brief picture of detachment and reverence.
shortened: Through divine power and heavenly grace they arose to educate the souls of nations and reform the world. They recline upon the cushions of detachment and hold fast to the fear of God. Neither self nor desire prevented them from drawing nigh to the supreme horizon nor held them back from turning toward it.

order.why: Read the realization of guidance through the whole person’s qualities.
Consider righteousness as the essence of holiness.
shortened: O thou pure soul! The essence of holiness is the characteristic of righteousness, for this is the highest aspiration of such as seek the threshold of God.

order.why: Read humility and lowliness alongside holiness.
shortened: Don the garments of holiness and adorn thy head with the crown of humility and lowliness before the dominion of the Lord of Hosts.

order.why: Bring the inquiry into movements, stillness, and everyday conduct.
Read education, freedom from passion, and heavenly attributes as a sustained practice.
shortened: Day and night He engaged in divine counsels and exhortations, guiding all to that which leads to humanity's eternal glory, so that souls might be trained to become manifestations of divine sanctification and holiness, and dawning-places of the lights of piety in the human world - even avoiding the slightest transgression, seeking freedom from the snares of self and passion, conforming all deeds and actions to the decisive divine texts, and adorning the human world with heavenly attributes, so that this world might become another world and this earthly realm might be transformed into a celestial domain.

order.why: Consider worship and remembrance as purifying waters.
shortened: In all gatherings and all lands, guide souls to worship and engagement in the remembrance of God, so that through these purifying waters, souls may day by day increase in purity of heart and sanctification of spirit, become manifestations of piety, and arise with what is necessary, fitting and worthy of the Day of the Covenant in terms of inner and outer purity and sanctification of spirit and heart.

order.why: Read purification of the heart through the image of an inscription.
shortened: The heart must needs be purified with the water of the fear of God, that it may be adorned with the inscription of the blessed words "Verily I am God's."

order.why: Keep reverence and remembrance paired.
shortened: Say: We counsel thee to fear God and to remember Him - a remembrance which hath preceded all remembrance.

order.why: Consider undistracted remembrance as a form of pure fear.
Read sincerity and reverence in secret in the Bab’s account.
shortened: Fear God, O servants of God, and be in God's religion sincere, upon the truth, a witness.
Verily they who fear their Lord in secret -- they were before the All-Merciful and His friends, upon the truth, by the truth, in the precincts of the Gate, pure.

order.why: Keep the prayer’s strong language of awe before divine majesty.
shortened: O Thou the dread of Whom hath fallen upon all things, before the splendors of Whose face the countenances of all men are downcast, at the revelations of Whose sovereignty all necks have humbly bowed, to the ruling of Whose will all hearts have been subdued, the awfulness of Whose majesty hath caused the foundations of all things to tremble, and to the power of Whose authority the winds have been subjected!

order.why: Read the Bab’s cited promise of a way out and sufficient divine support.
Consider steadfastness in the Bab’s letter to an uncle.
Read guarding against doubtful matters as a protective practice.
Keep the source’s strong claims about early religious education attributed.
shortened: Repeatedly hath this blessed utterance been heard from Him: that which is, in the first place and in the primal rank, obligatory and essential for children is the teaching of the word of Divine Unity and the ordinances of God; for without these the fear of God is not attained, and in the absence thereof a myriad hateful deeds, unrecognized and unseemly, and words impure, come to be made manifest.

And at another time He said: fathers must exert their utmost endeavor in fostering the religiosity of their children; for if the children attain not, in the beginning, unto this first adornment, they will become heedless of obedience to their parents---an obedience which, in a certain station, is obedience unto God.

order.why: Read the reported relationship of piety to character.
Keep the reported counsel to avoid what is abhorrent to God.
shortened: Hearts must possess the fear of God. Man should endeavour to avoid that which is abhorrent unto God.

order.why: Consider good deeds, spiritual qualities, and reverence in a greeting.
Read the connection between deeds and nearness.
shortened: We counsel thee and My loved ones unto righteousness and goodly deeds and the fear of God, and unto that which will draw thee nigh unto God, thy Lord and the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Consider love of the Lord as adornment and possessions as a possible barrier.
shortened: Say: Adorn your heads with the turbans of the love of your Lord, the All-Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Beware lest what ye possess prevent you from God, from Whom hath appeared every wise command.

order.why: Follow the call to purify heart, tongue, and limbs.
Read righteousness through restraint of desire.
shortened: Blessed is he who holdeth fast to righteousness and restraineth his soul from desire.

order.why: Keep the rejection of desire as a ruling power in its theological context.
shortened: Say: O people, fear God with true fear, and associate not anything with Him, and call not upon any god besides God, and take not your vain desires as lords unto yourselves, if ye be aware.

order.why: Read the contrast of desire and the illumination of certitude.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! Fear ye God and follow not your desires when the horizon of the heaven of mystical knowledge hath been illumined with the Luminary of certitude.

order.why: Consider the call to follow guidance rather than desire.
shortened: Say: Fear ye God and follow not your desires. Follow Him Who mentioneth you for the sake of God, the Mighty, the Beautiful.

order.why: Read desire beside receptivity to light.
Retain the warning about desires altering creation’s face.
Read the brief counsel against idle fancies.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear God and follow not your idle fancies. Follow Him Who calls you to the straight path.

order.why: Consider the choice of righteousness over wicked conduct.
shortened: Put away what the people possess of wickedness and evil, holding fast unto righteousness and the fear of God.

order.why: Read the warning against paths of corruption.
Keep the direct prohibition of forbidden acts.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear ye God, and commit not that which hath been forbidden you.

order.why: Read sanctification in relation to the Book’s prohibitions.
Hear the concise call to refrain from unseemly action.
Keep the severe judgment concerning righteousness and deeds in its source’s voice.
shortened: They who have cast away righteousness and committed unseemly acts - these have no portion of this ocean which surgeth before the faces of religions.

order.why: Read the warning that conduct can nullify deeds.
shortened: He commandeth you to righteousness and piety, and forbiddeth you from that which would render your deeds null and void.

order.why: Consider righteousness and the commands of the Book together.
shortened: I counsel you, O people, to observe righteousness and to follow that which ye have been commanded in the Book of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Read commanded conduct as benefit and protection.
shortened: Say: Fear God and take hold of that which ye are commanded. It will profit you in all the worlds of His worlds and protect you from the evil of the calumniators.

order.why: Keep the warning about heedlessness and temporal preoccupation.
shortened: Yet We counsel thee to fear the one true God and follow the guidance of the Eternal, lest heedlessness overtake thee or temporal concerns preoccupy thee.

order.why: Read the specific counsel concerning whom to follow.
shortened: Fear God and follow not every heedless doubter.

order.why: Consider the rejection of following a stubborn oppressor.
Keep the warning to people of understanding in its religious vocabulary.
Read the swords-of-fancy image as an account of division.
shortened: Say: O people, fear ye God and cut not asunder the strength of His Cause with the swords of your idle fancies. Fear God and be God-fearing in His religion.

order.why: Keep the counsel on the Covenant in its particular theological context.
shortened: O people of the earth! Fear God, and follow not those who have violated God's Covenant and Testament when there came the Day which had been promised in the Books of God and inscribed in the hearts of them who are nigh unto Him.

order.why: Consider steadfastness during upheaval.
shortened: O My loved ones! We counsel you to fear God and to manifest supreme steadfastness in this Cause whereby souls have been perturbed and idols have lamented.

order.why: Read the greeting to those holding the cord of godliness.
shortened: Glory be upon you and upon those who have held fast to the cord of godliness whereby the Cause of God has been exalted throughout all ages.

order.why: Read the account of refusal and following others as the source presents it.
shortened: He hath commanded all to observe piety and that which will lead them to the ultimate goal, but they have turned away and objected, having followed every heedless and rejected one.

order.why: Keep the direct appeal concerning recognition of Revelation.
Read reverence, recognition, worship, and praise together.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear ye God, and turn not away disdainfully from His Revelation. Fall prostrate on your faces before God, and celebrate His praise in the daytime and in the night season.

order.why: Consider the appeal to divines to judge fairly.
shortened: O concourse of divines! Fear ye God, then judge with fairness concerning this Unlettered One, to Whom testify the Books of God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. The tongue of utterance in the Kingdom of knowledge declareth: O concourse of divines! Fear ye the one true God.

order.why: Read the images of calumny and dissension obstructing light.
shortened: O bondsmaid of the True One, the purified hem is soiled with the dust of the calumny of the accusers, and the lamp of the world is prevented from shedding light and illumination by the blowing of the winds of dissension.

order.why: Hear the prayer for return and restored reverence.
shortened: Most strange, utterly strange, are those souls who for the sake of a moment's pleasure deprive themselves of God's good-pleasure which is the cause of eternal life and everlasting bounty. We beseech God to assist them to return and to adorn them with the ornament of fear of God.

order.why: Retain the concise counsel and its exact wording about hearts and minds.
shortened: We counsel all the loved ones of God to observe the fear of God and that whereby hearts and minds are concealed.

order.why: Defines piety through faithfulness and conduct in accordance with divine counsels.
Read adherence to reverence as a mark of the stated station.
Hear the brief account of the true friends’ desire.
Retain the personal counsel of the Wronged One.
shortened: Wherefore doth this Wronged One counsel thee unto the fear of God. He directeth thee unto trustworthiness and sincerity. Be characterized by this twain; embrace these two qualities.

order.why: Keep righteousness and fear of God paired.
shortened: We counsel all to fear God and to righteousness.

order.why: Read the call toward an elevated human station.
shortened: Say: O servants of the Most Merciful! The Wronged One counsels you to fear God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting, and to that whereby your station may be exalted in the world.

order.why: Consider the greeting and the exaltation of the Word.
Read chastity and reverence within the announcement.
Close the linked passages with the stated elevation of existence.
Read the supplied pilgrim-note question and answer as a distinct account of fear and love.
Consider the supplied letter on discipline, love, fear, and mercy with its stated attribution.
Keep the supplied provisional wisdom passage separate from the linked rendering.
Read the supplied Ecclesiastes excerpt with its original inline citation.
Close with the supplied Quranic passage’s practical virtues; retain its supplied citation, while comparative reading [1] identifies the parallel passage as 2:177.

questions: How can fear of God become a source of courage in the face of worldly power?
What do the passages on justice, punishment, mercy, and loving-kindness reveal about different motives for doing what is right?
How does an inward guardian of conduct differ from concern for reputation or legal consequences?
How does Qur’an 2:177 connect devotion with the needs of other people, fidelity, and endurance?
What might help religious education cultivate both moral restraint and confidence in divine mercy?
Which everyday practices would make reverence visible as truthfulness, fairness, generosity, and care?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 2:177 · Faith expressed in conduct
references.note: Read Pickthall’s translation of the passage joining belief, worship, giving, fidelity, and patience. Compare its practical account of righteousness with the compilation’s inward guardian and outward virtues. This is the parallel passage to the supplied Quranic quotation; that quotation’s original reference reads 2:172 and has been retained as supplied.

subjects.displayTitle: Two kinds of knowledge: from information to insight
subjects.introduction: Knowing that honey exists puts no sweetness on the tongue. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s homely example marks the distance between knowledge held as description and knowledge that has been tasted, and it opens a cluster of distinctions worth keeping apart: sight and insight, the sensible and the intelligible, learning acquired in schools and the light God casts into a heart. None of them belittles study. Science, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá insists, is the discoverer of realities, and material and divine learning are the two wings on which humanity flies; the trouble of the age is that one wing has outgrown the other. Bahá’u’lláh adds a sterner test. Knowledge that wells from divine inspiration bears patience, longing, understanding and love; knowledge driven by selfish desire yields only arrogance and conceit, and can become the thickest veil between a person and God. James likewise asks that wisdom be judged by its fruits, gentleness and peace rather than envy and strife [1]. To know, then, is finally to be changed, and greed or an unkind word can close the inner eye as easily as a scrap of paper shuts the outer one. The path leads on into the harmony of science and religion, the difference between intelligible and perceptible realities, and the recognition of God that all true knowing serves.
subjects.arc: Begin with knowing and tasting, affirm investigation and complementary learning, distinguish kinds of perception, then examine receptivity, limits, and the moral fruits of knowledge.

order.why: Distinguish sensible and intelligible realities and the images used to express them.
shortened: There is a point that is pivotal to grasping the essence of the other questions that we have discussed or will be discussing, namely, that human knowledge is of two kinds.
One is the knowledge acquired through the senses. That which the eye, the ear, or the senses of smell, taste, or touch can perceive is called "sensible".
The other kind of human knowledge is that of intelligible things; that is, it consists of intelligible realities which have no outward form or place and which are not sensible.
But when you undertake to express these intelligible realities, you have no recourse but to cast them in the mould of the sensible, for outwardly there is nothing beyond the sensible.

order.why: Open with the reported difference between knowing honey exists and tasting it.
shortened: Knowledge and comprehension of the realities of things is impossible except through divine wisdom, for knowledge is of two kinds: conceptual and realized--in other words, acquired and immediate.
For example, man knows that honey exists in the world, but this conception alone does not suffice and yields no sweet taste--rather, he must taste it for experiential knowledge to be obtained.

order.why: Read the two wings and the explicit need for material and spiritual science.
shortened: Scientific knowledge is the highest attainment upon the human plane, for science is the discoverer of realities. It is of two kinds: material and spiritual. Material science is the investigation of natural phenomena; divine science is the discovery and realization of spiritual verities. The world of humanity must acquire both. A bird has two wings; it cannot fly with one. Material and spiritual science are the two wings of human uplift and attainment.

order.why: Keep praise of natural investigation beside the call to reason about divine questions.
shortened: The field and scope of natural philosophy have been greatly enlarged, and its accomplishments are most praiseworthy, for it has served humanity. But according to the evidence of present world conditions divine philosophy -- which has for its object the sublimation of human nature, spiritual advancement, heavenly guidance for the development of the human race, attainment to the breaths of the Holy Spirit and knowledge of the verities of God -- has been outdistanced and neglected.

In divine questions we must not depend entirely upon the heritage of tradition and former human experience; nay, rather, we must exercise reason, analyze and logically examine the facts presented so that confidence will be inspired and faith attained.

order.why: Consider the hope for spiritual development alongside university learning.
shortened: As material and physical sciences are taught here and are constantly unfolding in wider vistas of attainment, I am hopeful that spiritual development may also follow and keep pace with these outer advantages. As material knowledge is illuminating those within the walls of this great temple of learning, so also may the light of the spirit, the inner and divine light of the real philosophy glorify this institution.

order.why: Read increased vision as a guide to understanding.
Consider the prayer for penetrating insight and renewed perception.
shortened: Beseech the peerless and incomparable Lord to bestow a penetrating insight upon His servants, for insight leadeth to true knowledge and is conducive to salvation. Indeed, the attainments of man's understanding are dependent upon his keenness of sight. Were the children of men to gaze with the eye of understanding, they would see the world illumined with a new light in this day.

order.why: Bring the veil of greed and envy into the inquiry.
shortened: O children of understanding! If the eyelid, however delicate, can deprive man's outer eye from beholding the world and all that is therein, consider then what would be wrought if the veil of covetousness were to descend upon his inner eye. Say: O people! The darkness of greed and envy becloudeth the radiance of the soul even as the clouds obstruct the light of the sun.

order.why: Read the reported thin-paper demonstration and the effects of an unkind word.
Examine the Book of Certitude’s distinction through patience, love, arrogance, and recognition.
shortened: Know verily that Knowledge is of two kinds: Divine and Satanic. The one welleth out from the fountain of divine inspiration; the other is but a reflection of vain and obscure thoughts. The source of the former is God Himself; the motive-force of the latter the whisperings of selfish desire. The one is guided by the principle: "Fear ye God; God will teach you"; the other is but a confirmation of the truth: "Knowledge is the most grievous veil between man and his Creator." The former bringeth forth the fruit of patience, of longing desire, of true understanding, and love; whilst the latter can yield naught but arrogance, vainglory and conceit.

order.why: Connect true learning with restraint from harmful conduct.
shortened: The truly learned one is he whose knowledge prevents him from all that My good-pleasure and His good-pleasure abhorreth, and the mature one is he who hath attained unto the dawning-place of My knowledge; and apart from this none is mature, even though he may live for [many] years.

order.why: Contrasts knowledge received from God with acquired learning.
Keep the reported moral criticism of philosophers attributed and attend to its test of lives.
shortened: The greatest philosophers without this Spirit are powerless, their souls lifeless, their hearts dead! Unless the Holy Spirit breathes into their souls, they can do no good work.
Learned philosophers, unenlightened by the Divine Spirit, have often been men of inferior morality; they have not proclaimed in their actions the reality of their beautiful phrases.
The difference between spiritual philosophers and others is shown by their lives.

order.why: Consider the difference between collecting knowledge and recognizing its object.
Read the Hidden Words’ two eyes as an invitation concerning attention.
shortened:
12. O MAN OF TWO VISIONS!
Close one eye and open the other. Close one to the world and all that is therein, and open the other to the hallowed beauty of the Beloved.

order.why: Read the reported examples of sense perception and intellectual realities.
shortened: Likewise, the perceptions of man are of two kinds: sensible and intelligible. But the perceptions of the animal are of one kind only: the sensible. For it is established that the animal apprehendeth nothing save the sensible. Man, however, hath two perceptions: one, sensible perception, as when he seeth the lamp as a lamp; the other, intelligible perception, such as mathematical truths, the sphericity of the earth, and the centrality of the sun.

order.why: Keep the concise reported distinction between senses and reason.
Consider inner perception as apprehending beyond physical sight.
Read the contrast of optical errors and insight in the source’s own terms.
Consider temporal sight and the enduring vision of the Kingdom.
Keep the reported distinction between observing and apprehending, with its omission.
shortened: Sight is physical; insight is ideal. There are many people who have the power of sight but they lack insight. Insight perceives and unfolds the spiritual susceptibilities of consciousness. It discerns the realities of phenomena. Sight is the faculty of observing things but it is not the apprehender of things. Insight becomes cognizant of the real state of things and piercing through the veil of appearances it goes to the very heart of a given object...

order.why: Read the public address’s paired outer and inner faculties as gifts.
Distinguish the spirit’s operation through organs and without them.
Read the reported dream example as part of that argument.
shortened: The spirit has two modes of operation: one through instruments and means, that is, seeing through the eye, hearing through the ear, speaking through the tongue.
The other operation is without instruments, as in the world of dreams where one sees without eyes, hears without ears, speaks without tongue, and travels without moving the feet.

order.why: Consider the public address’s argument from sleeping body and perceiving spirit.
Read the Manifestations’ knowledge with the preceding question and distinction of intuition and conception.
shortened: Question: What are the limitations imposed upon the powers of the Manifestations of God and, in particular, upon their knowledge?
Answer: Knowledge is of two kinds: existential knowledge and formal knowledge--that is, intuitive knowledge and conceptual knowledge.

The knowledge that people generally have of things consists in conceptualization and observation, that is, either the object is conceived through the rational faculty, or through its observation a form is produced in the mirror of the heart. The scope of this knowledge is quite limited, as it is conditioned upon acquisition and attainment.

order.why: Keep the universal divine Intellect distinct from the human power of investigation.
shortened: But the universal divine Intellect, which transcends nature, is the outpouring grace of the pre-existent Power. It encompasses all existing realities and receives its share of the lights and mysteries of God. It is an all-knowing power, not a power of investigation and sensing. The spiritual power associated with the world of nature is the power of investigation, and it is through investigation that it discovers the realities and properties of things. But the heavenly intellectual power, which is beyond nature, encompasses, knows and comprehends all things, is aware of the divine mysteries, truths and inner meanings, and discovers the hidden verities of the Kingdom.

order.why: Read the distinction between human discoveries and divine realities.
shortened: Concerning the matter of spiritual discoveries that you mentioned, the human spirit has a comprehensive power over the realities of things.

Thus it is evident that the human spirit has comprehensive power and control over the realities of things, and discovers secrets hidden in the realm of this world. But the Divine Spirit discovers divine realities and universal mysteries in the heavenly realm.

order.why: Consider the reported identification of intuition with Divine Universal Reason.
shortened: Likewise, the outward faculties and senses of man discover and perceive the appearance of things. But the light of Intuition (or Inner Perception) is a light which comprehends the realities and the core of things. Intuition (or Inner Perception) means the Divine Universal Reason, and it comprehends and grasps supernatural things and conditions which cannot be grasped by the outward senses.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast of intellectual and divine light attributed.
shortened: The light of the intellect enables us to understand and realize all that exists, but it is only the Divine Light that can give us sight for the invisible things, and which enables us to see truths that will only be visible to the world thousands of years hence.

order.why: Distinguish essential knowledge from knowledge in the realm of action.
Read the parallel account of divine knowledge, retaining its internal omission.
shortened: Furthermore, knowledge is of two kinds: One knowledge relates to the Divine Essence - it is essential divine knowledge, identical with the Essence, not distinct from it, for in that station there is pure unity, and the Essence comprises all names and attributes.
The other knowledge is in the realm of action, meaning it is identical with what is known, and that is realization externally.

order.why: Make the limits of knowledge of essence explicit.
shortened: As our knowledge of things, even of created and limited ones, is of their attributes and not of their essence, how then can it be possible to understand in its essence the unbounded Reality of the Divinity? For the inner essence of a thing can never be known, only its attributes. For example, the inner reality of the sun is unknown, but it is understood through its attributes, which are heat and light. The inner essence of man is unknown and unfathomed, but it is known and characterized by its attributes.

order.why: Read the counsel to begin with rational arguments for an audience requiring them.
Consider the public address’s account of philosophical schools and rational proofs.
Keep the account of Socrates attributed to the Tablet to Dr Forel.
shortened: Now concerning philosophers, they are of two schools. Thus Socrates the wise believed in the unity of God and the existence of the soul after death; as his opinion was contrary to that of the narrow-minded people of his time, that divine sage was poisoned by them.

order.why: Read the reported difference between knowing attributes and seeking foundational proof.
Keep the distinct pairings of error and guidance, bodies and religions.
shortened: O dervish, know that knowledge is of two kinds: one is error and one is guidance. Error is the portion of the ignorant.
Furthermore, He says: "Knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge of bodies and knowledge of religions."

order.why: Consider the reported distinction of philosophical conclusions and spiritual guidance.
Read the reported schools of philosophy and the mirror of meditation.
shortened: They divided Divine philosophy into two parts: one kind is that of which the knowledge can be acquired through lectures and study in schools and colleges. The second kind of philosophy was that of the Illuminati, or followers of the inner light.
To illustrate this, think of man as endowed with two kinds of sight; when the power of insight is being used the outward power of vision does not see.
The meditative faculty is akin to the mirror; if you put it before earthly objects it will reflect them. Therefore if the spirit of man is contemplating earthly subjects he will be informed of these.

But if you turn the mirror of your spirits heavenwards, the heavenly constellations and the rays of the Sun of Reality will be reflected in your hearts, and the virtues of the Kingdom will be obtained.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison of induction and prophetic sight in its own imagery.
Read universal and special teachers as a distinction of educational scope.
shortened: Teachers are of two kinds: universal and special. The universal Instructors are the Prophets of God, and the special teachers are the philosophers. The philosophers are capable of educating and training a limited circle of human souls, whereas the holy, divine Manifestations of God confer general education upon humanity.

order.why: Consider the material and moral functions of two civilizations.
Read the reported complementary modes of material and spiritual progress.
shortened: Progress is of two kinds: material and spiritual. The former is attained through observation of the surrounding existence and constitutes the foundation of civilization. Spiritual progress is through the breaths of the Holy Spirit and is the awakening of the conscious soul of man to perceive the reality of Divinity.

order.why: Hear the invitation to discover both physical and divine truths.
shortened: Depend thou on this, and abandon every imagination and be attracted to the light of reality and discover both the divine truths and physical truths!

order.why: Read the hope that intellectual discoveries may be joined by knowledge of the Kingdom.
shortened: Just as human intellects have revealed the secrets of matter and have brought forth from the realm of the invisible the mysteries of nature, may minds and spirits, likewise, come into the knowledge of the verities of God, and the realities of the Kingdom be made manifest in human hearts.

order.why: Consider the Sun of Reality as an image of education and growth.
Read general and particular education through the divine name Lord.
Keep knowledge and faith together as wings of ascent.
Consider knowledge, insight, faith, and love united in consciousness.
Read the relation of purification and the opening of knowledge.
shortened: Likewise, ask thou of God that the magnet of His love should draw unto thee the knowledge of Him. Once a soul becometh holy in all things, purified, sanctified, the gates of the knowledge of God will open wide before his eyes.

order.why: Consider effort and the fountain of knowledge in understanding scriptural symbols.
shortened: Endeavor with thy soul, so that the fountain of knowledge may flow within thy heart and the bounties of mysteries may pour upon thee from the Kingdom of Lights. Then thou wilt understand the meanings hidden and recorded in the symbols in the Holy Scriptures.

order.why: Read the invitation to contemplate realities and scriptural allegories.
Keep the city of knowledge and the clarity of spiritual allusions in their mystical setting.
shortened: For otherwise, unto them that have recognized the Repositories of divine Revelation and beheld through His inspiration the mysteries of divine authority, all the verses of God are perspicuous and all His allusions are clear. Such men discern the inner mysteries that have been clothed in the garment of words as clearly as ye perceive the heat of the sun or the wetness of water, nay even more distinctly.

order.why: Read the movement beyond the Valley of Knowledge into unity.
shortened: 35 After passing through the Valley of Knowledge, which is the last station of limitation, the wayfarer cometh to the FIRST STATION OF UNITY and drinketh from the cup of oneness, and gazeth upon the manifestations of singleness. In this station he pierceth the veils of plurality, fleeth the realms of the flesh, and ascendeth unto the heaven of unity. With the ear of God he heareth; with the eye of God he beholdeth the mysteries of divine creation.

order.why: Consider the interpretation of sight, hearing, and life in the miracles of Christ.
shortened: Consider that Christ reckoned as dead those who were nonetheless outwardly and physically alive; for true life is life eternal and true existence is spiritual existence. Thus if the Sacred Scriptures speak of raising the dead, the meaning is that they attained everlasting life; if they say that one who was blind was made to see, the meaning of this seeing is true insight; if they say that one who was deaf was made to hear, the meaning is that he acquired an inner ear and attained spiritual hearing.

order.why: Keep the reported discussion of Nicodemus and spiritual comprehension attributed.
shortened: A little child cannot understand or comprehend the words of a man of twenty years. Those who have human minds cannot understand and comprehend the heavenly mind, any more than a child can comprehend a man's mind or words. Christ's teachings were heavenly, and we must have a heavenly mind in order to comprehend them. The mind of Nicodemus bore the same relation to the teachings of Jesus that a child's mind bears to the man's mind which is, in a sense, perfect.

order.why: Read the reported scriptural allusion and its promise of healing.
Hear the address to a person without physical sight affirming spiritual perception.
shortened: O thou possessor of a seeing heart! Although, materially speaking, thou art deprived of physical sight, yet, praise be to God, spiritual insight is thine. Thy heart seeth and thy spirit heareth. Bodily sight is subject to a thousand maladies and assuredly will ultimately be lost. Thus no importance should be attached to it. But the sight of the heart is illumined. It discerneth and discovereth the divine Kingdom. It is everlasting and eternal.

order.why: Read the brief companion affirmation of spiritual vision.
Keep Isaac and Jacob as the source’s illustrations of seeing.
Consider the eye of the heart and soul in relation to an unseen light.
Read the continuing illumination after the Sun’s setting.
Keep the reported blindness analogy as spiritual rhetoric, not a judgment of disability.
shortened: Such has always been the mystery of the days of God's Manifestations. A person with eyes and face can see stars millions of miles away, but a blind person cannot even see the sun, despite its light and warmth."

order.why: Read the reported contrast of heavenly and earthly states in its audience-specific address.
shortened: All are blind but you are endowed with sight. All are earthly but you are heavenly. Although you live on earth, you soar high in heaven.

order.why: Retain the severe theological judgment about mystical insight in the source’s voice.
shortened: Not everyone who has the form of a human being is worthy of the Most Great Panorama, nor will such a one necessarily be accounted a human being before God. For all who remain bereft of the robe of mystical insight are reckoned as beasts of the field by God.

order.why: Read the contrasting inclinations of human beings in their spiritual terms.
Consider the reported distinction between livelihood-seeking and heavenly mind.
Consider reported physical bonds and spiritual fraternity.
shortened: Earthly fraternity is due either to a family relationship, or to a commercial bond, or to a bond of love based upon policy or politics, or to a racial bond which supplies that affection, or to a bond patriotic in foundation. These are physical susceptibilities and ordinary outward love. But spiritual susceptibilities, namely, real love and heavenly fraternity, emanate through divine channels. They emanate from faith, or they emanate from knowledge, or they emanate from the bounty of the Holy Spirit, or they emanate from the effulgence of the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between bodily and spiritual health.
Read the reported North Pole comparison without treating its historical attribution as verified history.
shortened: We must endeavor to discover the world of humanity and the mysteries hidden in the reality of man. Although the discovery of the North Pole was an important matter--I do not mean to abase this effort; it was a great endeavor achieved by Mr. Peary--yet the purpose is this: If he had discovered the mysteries of the Kingdom, he could train some souls who would be able to discover all the poles; the physical pole as well as the spiritual pole; the earthly as well as the heavenly pole.

order.why: Consider the reported widening of comprehension and capacity.
Read the station of humanity through insight and knowledge.
shortened: Pure praise and the essence of glorification befit the sacred and holy court of the Intended One, Who created all existence with a single word and distinguished man through insight and knowledge above all else.

And the intent of this insight is not the outward sight which other than man also possesses, rather it is that insight which has dawned from the shining lights of the Sun of the word "He comprehendeth all vision." How lofty is the station of man if he attains to its conditions and becomes aware of its degrees!

order.why: Keep sight and knowledge paired as brilliant stars.
shortened: Praise be to the peerless Lord Who hath illumined the heaven of man's station with two brilliant stars - sight and knowledge.

order.why: Consider the distinction between derived and inherent light.
Read heavenly wisdom as a first bestowal.
Keep recognition of the newly arrived Friend in new attire central to this source.
shortened: Great is the station of him who hath in this Day perceived and become aware of the truth, and wretched is he who hath failed to comprehend the utterances of the Lord of wisdom and to recognize the newly-arrived Friend in His new attire.

order.why: Read the appeal to fairness and proof within its account of Revelation.
shortened: He hath come with the hosts of divine revelation and inspiration, and hath manifested that which lay hidden in the treasuries of His knowledge and stored in the repositories of His might. Thereupon the servants and dwellers of the lands rose up in rejection and protest, to such extent that they denied the Books of God and His Scriptures and whatsoever was revealed aforetime unto His Prophets and Messengers. Say: O people of the earth! Be fair in the name of God - if ye deny this Most Great Cause and this Mighty Announcement, by what proof can ye establish that which ye possess?

order.why: Consider insight joined to pondering earlier ages.
shortened: Praise be to God that ye have drunk from the ocean of divine knowledge of the All-Merciful and received your portion from the Sun of God's love.

How excellent is the state of one who sees with insight and the condition of one who ponders on past ages. Should a soul attain but a drop from the ocean of wisdom, surely neither the world nor aught within it would deter him from the Straight Path and the Strong Cord.

order.why: Read the ocean of knowledge and its branching gulfs.
Keep the drop of divine knowledge and turning toward the goal in its mystical imagery.
Consider distinct nourishment for spirit and body.
Read insight as a gift exceeding worldly treasure.
shortened: They who have been given insight by God are such as would not exchange it for the treasures of the heavens and earth, could ye but know it.

order.why: Hear the image of knowledge raining upon a discerning heart.
shortened: Through Him the clouds of the will of your Lord, the All-Merciful, rain down the showers of knowledge upon the heart of every discerning believer.

order.why: Consider illumination through the lamp of knowledge.
Read the brief praise of the dawning light of guidance.
shortened: O thou who hast believed in God and been guided! The light of guidance hath dawned from the dayspring of eternity--glorified be my Lord, the Most High!

order.why: Keep recognition, certainty, and divine assistance together in the congratulatory address.
shortened: O servant of Baha! How wonderful, how wonderful that you have turned to the manifest light and drunk from the fountain of certitude and attained unto true certainty and achieved recognition of the Lord God and been confirmed in receiving the gift of the Forgiver.

order.why: Consider teaching through the garden and nightingale images.
shortened: Adorn the meadow of guidance, make to grow the flowers of inner meanings, and place the crown of bounty upon the head of the nightingale of the spirit. Call the spiritual nightingales to sing their songs and teach them the realities and meanings.

order.why: Read knowledge brought into gatherings and utterance.
shortened: And you, O lamp within which is lit the light of the love of God, shine forth with the light of knowledge in the gatherings of utterance, that the mystery of exposition may be revealed in human reality, and eyes may be illumined by witnessing the signs of your Lord, and ears may comprehend words that are the Mother of the Book, and spirits may be stirred by fragrant breaths wafting from the direction of God's gift.

order.why: Hear the prayer for illumined eyes and inner vision.
shortened: O Lord! Illumine their eyes with the light of Thy knowledge and brighten their inner vision with the radiance of beholding the signs of Thy oneness.

order.why: Read the prayer that all may share in knowledge and insight.
shortened: We beseech God to grant success to all, that they may not remain deprived of the ocean of knowledge and bereft of the kingdom of insight.

order.why: Close the linked readings with gratitude for guidance and the rain of mercy.
Read the supplied distinction of objective and subjective faith as a separate classification.
shortened: Know that faith is of two kinds. The first is objective faith that is expressed by the outer man, obedience of the limbs and senses. The other faith is subjective, and unconscious obedience to the will of God.

But the discerning faith that consists of true knowledge of God and the comprehension of divine words, of such faith there is very little in any age. That is why His Holiness Christ said to His followers, "Many are called but few are chosen."

order.why: Keep the supplied learning-and-recognition passage with its original terminology.
Read the supplied provisional account of essential knowledge separately from the linked version.
shortened: Knowledge is of two kinds. The one is the knowledge that pertaineth to the Essence [dhat]. This knowledge is of God and is identical with and undistinguishable from His Essence, for it ariseth from the station of His Supreme Singleness in which His Essence encompasseth all Names and Attributes. That Essential knowledge is divine and sanctified above all understanding. The other kind of knowledge is confined to the plane of action and visible being. In other words, it ariseth from that which is revealed and manifest, and signifieth the outward realization of a thing.

order.why: Consider the supplied provisional account of inherent and empirical knowledge.
shortened: Those who have been initiated into the divine mysteries believe that knowledge is of two kinds: The first is the comprehension of a thing without the conception of it in the mind; this is essential or inherent knowledge [dhati]. The second is empirical knowledge [suri], and that is knowledge acquired through observation which consisteth of the comprehension of a thing perceived as an image in the mind. Saying that God beheld [His creation] referreth to observational knowledge, whereas existential knowledge is identical with His Essence, the Essence of Divinity itself, whose reality is at once unknowable and unfathomable to all.

order.why: Keep the supplied threefold classification and explanation of imagery with its omission.
shortened: All human understanding and knowledge is of three categories. One is the knowledge of abstract concepts and universal elemental realities which are comprehended by sound minds and holy souls. Another consisteth of the ideal forms and images of external entities perceivable by the physical senses and faculties. And the third is that category of knowledge which is under the influence of both mental and sensuous powers, in other words thoughts produced by concepts that assume the shape of concrete things in such a way as to be visible to the faculty of imagination as well as understood by the intellect. Since the radiant flame of the divine intellect that discerneth abstract verities is obscured in all human beings, and since people's perceptions are limited to the tangible, the third type of knowledge is often adopted to explain these realities, so that feeble minds may, to some extent, partake of spiritual truths.

order.why: Read the supplied provisional Bab passage on limitation and unity.
Consider the supplied Quranic question about rain, growth, and vision.
Keep the supplied John of the Cross comparison concerning a small obstruction.
Read the supplied Plotinus invitation to another way of seeing.
Keep the supplied Pseudo-Dionysius distinction of intellectual faculty and communion.
Read the supplied Ghazali account of outward and inward eyes.
Consider the supplied Plotinus question about describing the simple, retaining its omissions.
End with the supplied invitation to read the universe as an open book.

questions: What changes when knowledge moves from description to experience, as in the example of honey?
Which different meanings of two kinds of knowledge appear here, and what confusion arises if they are treated as one distinction?
How can material investigation and spiritual learning strengthen one another in a person or institution?
How does James 3:13–18 invite us to assess wisdom through its effects on conduct and relationships?
What practices might expose the influence of greed, envy, pride, or habit on what we think we see?
How can confidence in the possibility of insight coexist with humility about the limits of human comprehension?

references.label: 1 · James 3:13–18 · Wisdom known by its fruits
references.note: Read the King James Version’s contrast between wisdom joined to envy and strife and wisdom expressed through gentleness, mercy, and peace. Compare this with the Book of Certitude’s account of the fruits of knowledge. Keep this moral distinction separate from the compilation’s other distinctions concerning perception, experience, and divine knowledge.

subjects.displayTitle: Empty learning: when words must become life
subjects.introduction: People know the name of the Lamp, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá once remarked, and repeat it constantly, without the least idea that a lamp is meant to give light. Learning can fail in exactly that way, and so can worship. Bahá’u’lláh draws the line sharply: sciences that begin with words and end with words have never been of any worth, while those that bear fruit for the well-being of people are acceptable to God. A man seats himself among the sandals by the door while coveting the seat of honour; another lays claim to inner knowledge and deeper knowledge hidden within it; a third washes the feet of all mankind and worships on every mountain, yet without sincerity none of it is accepted. The Dhammapada makes the same point with a herdsman counting another man’s cattle: reciting the teaching is not living it [1]. The invitation is demanding, to ask whether what we know has made us more useful, more truthful, more awake. The path continues through hypocrisy and pride, the claim to inner knowledge, and the question of what makes a religious practice sincere.
subjects.arc: Begin with the lamp and the fruits of useful knowledge, examine sincerity and the dangers of display, then read historical critiques in context and return to recognition and responsible practice.

order.why: Examine ambition disguised as humility, useful knowledge, and sincerity in worship.
shortened: Amongst the people is he who seateth himself amid the sandals by the door whilst coveting in his heart the seat of honour. Say: What manner of man art thou, O vain and heedless one, who wouldst appear as other than thou art?
We have permitted you to read such sciences as are profitable unto you, not such as end in idle disputation; better is this for you, if ye be of them that comprehend.

To none is it permitted to mutter sacred verses before the public gaze as he walketh in the street or marketplace; nay rather, if he wish to magnify the Lord, it behoveth him to do so in such places as have been erected for this purpose, or in his own home. This is more in keeping with sincerity and godliness.

order.why: Open with the reported lamp whose name is known but whose light is neglected.
Make the explicit approval of beneficial arts and sciences prominent.
shortened: By "arts and sciences" is meant those which begin with words and end with words. Such arts and sciences, however, as are productive of good results, and bring forth their fruit, and are conducive to the well-being and tranquility of men have been, and will remain, acceptable before God.

order.why: Read the call to learning that benefits both scholars and the wider community.
Read the reported test of a rosary through the character it helps cultivate.
Consider heartfelt thanksgiving beside words spoken by habit.
shortened: My heart is in a continual state of thanksgiving, and so often those accustomed to this form say the words with the lips merely, and their hearts are far from being in a state of thanksgiving.

order.why: Keep sciences and crafts joined to character and education.
shortened: Thereafter, efforts must be made to teach them sciences, crafts and knowledge to the extent possible, for without heavenly virtues and upright character, the mere acquisition of learning and arts will not suffice and will not prevent moral corruption and the harms of self and passion, but rather will become the cause of promoting false thoughts and a means of strengthening personal interests, unless accompanied by divine education.

order.why: Read the reported danger of knowledge serving oppression or division.
shortened: Conversely, if a person is deprived of divine virtues and spiritual education, their knowledge becomes an instrument of oppression - in the political realm turning celebration into battle, demolishing and destroying the foundation of comfort; in the religious realm promoting unsound opinions and false traditions, causing enmity and discord between human souls.

order.why: Consider learning directed toward its object and learning that feeds pride.
shortened: If, then, the pursuit of knowledge lead to the beauty of Him Who is the Object of all Knowledge, how excellent that goal; but if not, a mere drop will perhaps shut a man off from flooding grace, for with learning cometh arrogance and pride, and it bringeth on error and indifference to God.

order.why: Read the role of intention in years of worship, study, and contemplation.
Keep the concrete harm of false expertise before the reader.
shortened: The affliction of the world comes from the ignorant one who adorns himself with the ornament of knowledge and makes a show of it, for he forbids the helpless servants from that which benefits them and commands them to that which harms them.

order.why: Distinguish the reported criticism of irrational customs from divine principles.
Read the critique of speculative subjects absorbing students’ time and energy.
Consider the reported question of redirecting intellectual effort toward important matters.
Keep the account of jafr and the requirement of worthwhile results in context.
shortened: The science of jafr had currency in the Qur'anic Dispensation, but its derived principles were unknown, therefore correct results were not obtained. But in this Dispensation all are commanded not to pursue matters that do not yield great results.

order.why: Read the specific criticism of obsolete usulist disciplines.
Keep the historical account of frustrated students and its existing omission.
Attribute the reported judgment of Al-Azhar students to its particular historical source.
Read the reported verdict on an unproductive system as a specific assessment.
Consider the reported poet’s uncorrectable book as a story about fruitless labor.
Read the reported sermon and its unmoved audience.
shortened: The son, then going up the platform took as his text one of the most difficult verses of the Khoran and round it collected many subtle interpretations, philosophic axioms etc. The audience was not only not moved but was bored at such a dry sermon that the people instead listening to him began to speak amongst themselves.

order.why: Keep the reported wordplay about a guest within the observed gathering.
Read the positive image of pearls emerging from reason and wisdom.
shortened: A hundred thousand gleaming pearls can emerge in an instant from the shell of reason and wisdom, displaying their radiance in the market of the jewelers of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Consider the critique of unsupported inherited theories in its historical argument.
Keep the Bab’s judgment on conjecture within its revealed context.
Read the reported spider image of repeatedly rebuilt assumptions.
Consider the reported seeds sown in barren land.
Keep the reported warning to Sarah Farmer directed to that gathering’s purposes.
Read the reported bee comparison as a challenge to limited human ambition.
Consider a life consumed by anticipation of changing worldly fortunes.
Read the cold-iron image as a critique of unresponsive attention.
shortened: Such souls are like cold iron that is never affected by anything - even under hammer and anvil they show no effect, seek no realization, no thought, no depth of understanding, and desire nothing but worldly livelihood.

order.why: Distinguish remembrance and thought from their imagined objects.
shortened: O thou who speakest in praise of God!

The tongue must needs have remembrance and the minds must needs have thought. However, remembrances and thoughts are diverse and different. Some people occupy themselves with remembrance of imaginary truths and shadowy reflections. When these vain imaginings disappear and these shadowy reflections set, they are left frustrated and at a loss.

order.why: Keep the theological rejection of a mentally fashioned Inner Reality in its own voice.
Read the reported argument about worshipping a mental construction.
Consider the specific critique of the Sufi account of annihilation and essential temporality.
Keep the reported introduction to a Sufi story within its stated purpose.
Read the reported criticism of imagined travel outside the body without generalizing about a people.
shortened: Sometimes people imagine that they leave the body and travel in the sky, then return to the body. They think so. In India they are full of these ideas, and these are the cause of their downfall--because of their imaginations.

order.why: Consider the witnessed self-injury and rejection of its classification as a miracle.
Read the reply that redirects a claim about fire toward light.
Keep the judgment on ascetic disciplines in its theological setting.
Consider the difference between constant religious activity and awakened knowledge.
shortened: O thou who art the Ornament of the Mystics!

There are many worshippers and countless ascetics, yet few are truly wakeful to divine knowledge. One spends day and night in bowing and prostration, another lies dormant in the corner of piety and asceticism, another remains in the well of nature, heedless of the moon in the heights of truth, while yet another wanders occupied in the gardens of mathematical science, oblivious to the light of divine unity and the manifestation of the divine identity.

order.why: Read the account of claimed spiritual perception and its contradictory images.
shortened: Consider how many souls claimed knowledge and, in their own imagination, followed the spiritual path for years, yearning for the vision of a great one and awaiting the dawning of lights. They believed the sun of truth was manifest in mineral, plant and animal. From thorns they claimed to smell the fragrance of the rose garden, and from poison they claimed to taste the supreme honey.

order.why: Keep the sweeping critique of earlier mystics attributed to this source.
Read the account of failed spiritual claims and its polemical imagery.
Consider the source’s assessment of frustrated contemplation.
Keep the brief judgment about mystics and claimed truth in its context.
shortened: O thou who art aware of the mysteries of the Day of Resurrection!
The mystics have been gathered in the company of the ignorant, and those who claimed knowledge and truth have crept behind the veil of heedlessness.

order.why: Read the explicit exception for some dervishes alongside its wider criticism.
shortened: Most dervishes wander in the valley of heedlessness, save a few who, through the grace of the All-Merciful, have in this spiritual springtime been adorned with luminous robes. Despite their claims to maturity and mystical knowledge, most of this group remain veiled.

order.why: Keep the source’s judgment of a particular gathering attributed.
Read the reported fantastic accounts as the speaker presents them.
Keep the reported ship-fire story as an attributed illustration of harmful superstition.
Consider the reported confusion of outward forms with inward truth.
Read the reported diagnosis of religious pretense and livelihood.
Keep the severe judgment of places of worship in its source’s voice.
shortened: In this Day all the temples, mosques, churches and synagogues have become gathering-places of entertainment. Although they mention the name of God and spend time ostensibly in prayer and in communion and in fellowship with each other, in truth they are heedless of the actual Truth, are immersed in selfish lusts and desires, are occupied with their private fancies and aspirations. Their hearts are not pure and their souls are not radiant. They do not implore God with real sincerity nor pray to Him with true fervour. They do not develop spiritual sensibilities or attraction of conscience nor any real cordiality or genuine fellowship.

order.why: Read the reported concern about worship joined to amusement.
Retain the source’s judgment concerning a customary feast without adopting it as an editorial rule.
Consider the account of inherited imitation and a lifeless cry.
Read the reported objection to substituting a formula and fee for moral accountability.
shortened: For many years I have sinned against God and his servants. I have ransacked the houses, orphaned the children, burned the hearts and have committed all kinds of iniquities. Is the government of God so child-like as to forgive all my past sins with the repetition of a mere formula? Is his system of dispensing justice so loose? Be gone! Thou ignorant Mullah! Thou art telling me all these things to get ten Piastres as thy fee.

order.why: Keep the reported learned visitor’s indignation alongside his claim to understanding.
shortened: "Once a learned man journeyed to see me to receive my blessing, saying he knew and comprehended the Baha'i teachings.
He instantly flared with indignation and strode angrily about the room.

order.why: Retain the reported observer’s judgment within the anecdote’s preserved portion.
Read the poem’s forceful preference for honesty over religious hypocrisy.
shortened:
Be thou of the people of hell-fire,
but be not a hypocrite.

Be thou an unbeliever,
but be not a plotter.

Make thy home in taverns,
but tread not the path
of the mischief-maker.

Fear thou God,
but not the priest.

Give to the executioner thy head,
but not thy heart.

Let thine abode be under the stone,
but seek not the shelter of the cleric.

order.why: Consider the dyed-jackal image and the search for spiritual radiance.
Keep the critique of empty poetic praise distinct from a blanket editorial judgment of poetry.
Read parrots and hollow sound as images of uncomprehending repetition.
shortened: They mumble about sciences while remaining veiled from the effacement of the imaginary and the clarity of the known. They mutter about arts but know not what they say, as if they were parrots or the calf that had a hollow sound.

order.why: Consider the danger of guides whose appearance conceals harm.
Keep the reported sheep-and-cobra warning in its personal address.
Read the appeal against following claims without proof, evidence, or reason.
shortened: Strange it is that, despite such deeds, the divines of these regions and territories do not accept one another, each counting himself to be the most accomplished and most pious. Destruction be upon them and upon those who follow them without clear proof, or evidence, or testimony, or reason!

order.why: Consider the particular dispute about imitating the form of revealed verses.
Keep the reported warning against claims that create an inner and outer division.
Read the particular account of doubt arising from fabricated traditions.
Keep the severe bird and garden metaphors within the source’s polemic.
shortened: Despite this, a few crows have taken over the field and with their cawing and croaking have created such a disturbance in this meadow that they wish to turn this garden of the All-Merciful into a dark furnace, and this divine paradise into a satanic dungheap. They want to turn the grateful birds into despised vultures, and the zealous falcons into ungrateful crows. They wish to transform the parrots of the divine sugar-land into earthly graveyard crows, and turn the rose garden of inner meanings and truths into a thornfield of endless vices.

order.why: Read the warning about distracting tales and doubts in its stated spiritual framework.
shortened: And the second rank is preoccupation with tales and stories and narratives and allusions and casting doubts into weak hearts.
Know this much: that whatever you hear that is other than the remembrance of the Ancient Beauty is meant to occupy with that which profits not and heedlessness from the remembrance of God.

order.why: Consider the Bab’s counsel on inherited principles within its forceful address.
shortened: First, thou must purify thy heart from every principle thou hast received from thy scholars, for they have drawn from turbid springs flowing one into another, some rejecting others.

order.why: Read the wheat-sifter and scholar comparison within the Kitab-i-Badi’s argument.
shortened: And surely those whom ye consider possessed of insight are ignorant ones who have made claims to knowledge and wisdom. Hearken unto the words of the Primal Point and Universal Manifestation Who said that the sifter of wheat of the land of Sad donned the garment of leadership though he had not studied a single letter of knowledge, while Shaykh Muhammad Hasan, who penned five hundred thousand verses in the practice of devotion unto God, produced not a single word that might deliver him from the fire in the Day of Resurrection.

order.why: Keep the Traveller’s Narrative account of investigation, recognition, and its historical language.
Read the encouragement to an unlettered addressee and the wheat-cleaner example.
shortened: O thou who art turned to the Beauty of the All-Merciful! Though outwardly thou art not among the learned and hast not acquired what the divines of the nations have gained, yet praise God that thou art established upon the throne of great success. The Most Exalted One, may the spirit of all existence be a sacrifice unto Him, hath said that although Shaykh Muhammad Hasan had written three volumes on jurisprudence, he remained deprived, while the wheat-cleaner of Isfahan donned the robe of jurisprudence.

order.why: Keep the account of Mulla Ali of Kand’s learning and nonrecognition attributed.
shortened: Mulla 'Ali of Kand, who carried volumes of books and for years acquired sciences and arts which, in his own estimation, others were incapable and powerless to acquire, did not attain to the recognition of God, glorified be His majesty, and remained fixed and established in his own error.

order.why: Read the burden-of-learning image in the encounter with the Divine Word.
shortened: It hath been observed that a person who spent numbered years acquiring outward knowledge, upon hearing the Divine Word, fled as "asses fleeing from a lion," for it is indeed difficult for him to lay down his burden.

order.why: Consider knowledge and recognition of the Known in the source’s criterion.
shortened: He who has studied all branches of knowledge yet has failed to recognize Him Who is the Known is accounted as the most ignorant among men, and his name is not inscribed in the Preserved Tablet of glory. We have counseled all the manifestations of knowledge, one and all, not to hesitate in this Cause, even should they possess all the gems of wisdom and learning.

order.why: Read the contrast of learned and illiterate people in relation to recognition.
Keep the comparison of a shepherd and book learning in its particular theological voice.
shortened: He who tendeth sheep in the valleys and upon the mountains is, in the sight of God, superior to those who have perused the books of the world in the evenings and the mornings and during the nights and days.

order.why: Read the account of the truly learned person as an eye and spirit for humanity.
Consider knowledge itself as a possible barrier to its object.
shortened: Among them are those whom knowledge hath prevented from the Known One, and those whom vain imaginings have veiled from the horizon of certitude.

order.why: Read the counsel against learning becoming a veil.
shortened: Beware lest learning debar you from the Self-Subsisting or vain imaginings veil you from God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Describes learning and imagined mystical insight becoming veils.
Keep the concise warning about following a veiled learned person.
shortened: Say: O people! By God, that which had never appeared in creation hath now appeared, and the All-Merciful hath come with the kingdom of proof. Turn ye unto Him and follow not every veiled learned one.

order.why: Retain the judgment of those taken as learned in the source’s voice.
shortened: Those whom you have taken as men of learning are, by My life, worshippers of vain imaginings. They have no mention with God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

order.why: Read the criticism of divines with its explicit exception.
shortened: The ignorant ones of the earth who today are known as divines have been and continue to be the fountainhead of vain imaginings, except such as God hath willed, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Consider the positive call to behold truth with one’s own eyes.
Read the distinction between widely recognized learning and attained knowledge.
shortened: At all times and seasons the shrill voice of the Most Exalted Pen and the rustling of the Lote-Tree of the utmost boundary are raised up, yet the people of the mortal realm are deprived of hearing, for they have followed those who have ever been the dawning-places of idle fancies and vain imaginings. Many are the learned ones who are barred from true knowledge, while thou, through God's grace and loving-kindness, glory be to Him, hast attained unto it.

order.why: Keep the critique of the people of the Bayan and inherited traditions in its historical setting.
Consider the contrast between long worship and response to a Manifestation.
Read claimed mystical knowledge tested at the appearance of its object.
shortened: How many mystics who laid claim to mystical knowledge turned away when He Who conversed with God was seated upon the Throne of His Revelation, and thus found themselves deprived of the presence of the True Object of all knowledge.

order.why: Retain the brief account of earlier imaginings and deprivation.
Read the possibility that deeds themselves become a veil.
